posts.name: cajunjoel
posts.cooked:
Yes, this is an unfortunate side effect of the migration of the posts. They all look "unread" to everyone. 

To mark all posts as read: Use the "Forum Tools" drop-down at the bottom of each of the topic list pages (e.g. http://sentinelsofthemultiverse.com/forums/general-discussion). Choose "Mark all topics Read". So if you want to mark EVERYTHING as read, then you'd need to do this at most about a dozen times. 

Looks like the pagination is a bit ugly, but at least its wrapping properly now.

I've adjusted the fonts a bit, so at least the list pages look a bit better. And, for some reason, the icons on the forum list page looked nothing at all like those on the topics list page. So I added new ones. 

*UPDATE* Oh! You can hit that same drop-down on the list of all forums, too. That's convenient. :) Look for the drop-down at the bottom of: http://sentinelsofthemultiverse.com/forum

A forum migration is never fun (I think this is my 12th or so) and we know that the users get attached to how the system behaved before. We were not able to keep nor integrate the old forums into the new site, and we opted to migrate them entirely in order to consolidate things under one user login. posts.cooked:
Two methods I can think of to solve this.

First would be to switch from a tagline url to a unique id (either large number, or UUID (though the latter is probably overkill)).  Of course, that removes the tagline feature that if you can remember topic name, you can easily get to the topic simply by providing it's name, as well as when it appears as a link in another page, the potential visitors can easily get a preview of what the link will take them to.

The second solution would be to add a validator on posting a new topic that will compare the would be tagline with what taglines currently exist, in order to guarrentee it's uniqueness, and, if not unique, spit the new topic post back out saying that the topic cannot be posted as another topic with the same (or similar) already exists.
